For each intent: (A) prompt a hosted LLM to produce device-specific configuration; (B) run a deterministic verifier (NetKAT/MEV-style or reachability checker) to detect violations; (C) when verifier flags failures, iteratively generate repair prompts up to three rounds; (D) record final verifier outcome. Compare two arms: (1) ungated (no verifier feedback used for deployment) and (2) gated generate–verify–repair. Fix seeds, model temperature, prompt templates, and repair-prompt policy. Emulate deployment in a high-fidelity network emulator to validate select cases' runtime behaviours (reachability probes, ACL enforcement). Use the same LLM model and fixed decoding seeds where supported. Run deterministic verifier on all outputs and sample emulator validation for a stratified subset. Predefine grammar specifications, grounding data extraction method, and tokenizer constraint implementation; freeze these in a preregistration.","expected_data":"Per-intent per-condition records: prompt, model output, grammar-violation flags, parse success/failure, verifier pass/fail with violation types, grounding mismatches logged, sample emulator probe results, and generation latency/resource metrics.","primary_outcome":"Reduction in combined syntactic+semantic failure rate (fraction of outputs failing parse or verifier checks) for constrained+grounded condition versus unconstrained baseline.","analysis_outline":"Use paired proportion tests (McNemar or paired two-proportion z-test) across the three conditions. Perform subgroup analysis by CLI dialect complexity and intent type. Report examples of remaining failures to characterize residual error modes.","novelty_evidence_ids":["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6909831","https://openalex.org/W4415680272","https://openalex.org/W7161090530"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4400611559","https://openalex.org/W4416655698","doi:10.1002/nem.2313"],"risks":["Implementing reliable token-level constrained decoding across vendor CLI dialects is engineering-intensive and may be imperfect.","Schema grounding requires accurate device-state snapshots; stale or incorrect state may induce harmful edits.","Constrained decoding may increase generation latency and occasionally force safe refusals, reducing utility."],"estimated_model_calls":900},{"candidate_id":"d4b2c6e1","title":"Rollback Success and Recovery: Verifier-Gated vs Ungated Deployment in Emulated NetOps","research_question":"Does verifier-gated deployment of LLM-generated network changes improve rollback success and reduce outage duration compared to ungated deployment when rollbacks are invoked in an emulated network environment?","hypotheses":["Verifier-gated deployments will have a higher rollback-success rate (restore baseline reachability/ACL semantics) when rollbacks are invoked than ungated deployments.","When rollback is invoked, verifier-gated deployments will exhibit shorter median outage durations than ungated deployments due to smaller and more correctable change sets.","Large multi-device changes and syntactically invalid rollback scripts from the LLM predict rollback failure irrespective of gating.",""],"proposed_design":"Create a set of change-intent tasks (n=200) that vary in change size and risk. For each task, generate both a deployment script and a rollback script from the LLM. Randomly assign tasks to two arms: (1) verifier-gated deployment (deployment only allowed if pre-deployment verifier passes) and (2) ungated deployment. Deploy changes in an emulator; for a prespecified fraction (e.g., 40%) induce a failure condition that triggers invoking the generated rollback script. Record whether rollback fully restores the prerechange reachability matrix and ACL semantics, outage duration, and whether rollback script executed syntactically. Preregister rollback success definition, safety limits, and retry policies.","expected_data":"Per-change records: intent, generated deployment script, generated rollback script, verifier outcome pre-deploy, whether rollback was invoked, rollback execution logs, final reachability/ACL matrices, outage duration, change-size metrics (lines, devices), and root-cause notes for rollback failures.","primary_outcome":"Rollback success rate (fraction of invoked rollbacks that restore baseline reachability/ACL semantics) comparing verifier-gated versus ungated arms.","analysis_outline":"Compare rollback-success proportions with two-proportion z-test or Fisher's exact test and report 95% CIs. Compare outage durations using Mann–Whitney U. Fit logistic regression for rollback failure with predictors: change size, devices touched, verifier pass/fail, syntactic validity of rollback script. Conduct exploratory root-cause taxonomy for failed rollbacks and report representative failure transcripts.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W7164168895","https://openalex.org/W7161165783","https://openalex.org/W7117986201"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4400611559","doi:10.1145/3808318","https://openalex.org/W4415680272"],"risks":["Emulator snapshot/restore fidelity may not reflect production stateful behaviours, biasing rollback success upward.","LLM-generated rollback scripts might omit side-effects (e.g., BGP route scoop/withdraw timing) not modeled in emulator.","Ungated deployments could create destructive conditions in shared resources; enforce strict emulator-only execution and safety cutoffs."],"estimated_model_calls":1200},{"candidate_id":"b8e5f037","title":"Adversarial Prompt Robustness and Effectiveness of Verifier-Based Guarding","research_question":"How susceptible are LLM-driven NetOps pipelines to adversarial/jailbreak prompts that produce unsafe configurations, and how effective is a deterministic verifier+policy-based guarded-execution pipeline at blocking these unsafe outputs prior to deployment?","hypotheses":["Adversarially crafted prompts adapted to NetOps contexts will induce unsafe configuration outputs at a higher rate than benign operational prompts.","A verifier+policy gated pipeline will block the majority of adversarially-induced unsafe outputs prior to deployment, substantially reducing emulator-observed unsafe deployments.","Some adversarial outputs will bypass simple syntactic/policy filters but be caught by deeper semantics-aware deterministic verification (reachability/policy violations)."],"proposed_design":"Curate two prompt corpora (n=150 benign intents; n=150 adversarial/jailbreak-style prompts constructed following documented jailbreak techniques adapted for NetOps). For each prompt, collect LLM outputs under three mitigation conditions: (1) no mitigation, (2) syntax/policy filter, (3) verifier+policy gated execution. For outputs accepted for deployment under each condition, optionally emulate deployment to confirm unsafe consequences. Use adjudicators (two independent) to label ambiguous cases. Predefine adversarial construction rules, policy definitions for 'unsafe', and adjudication protocol; preregister the plan and inter-rater rules.","expected_data":"Per-prompt records: prompt text, LLM output, mitigation condition, mitigation accept/reject, verifier detection flags, adjudicator label (unsafe/safe/ambiguous), emulator deployment result for accepted outputs (if executed), and time-to-detection.","primary_outcome":"Mitigation detection effectiveness: proportion of adversarial unsafe outputs blocked by verifier+policy gating versus no-mitigation baseline.","analysis_outline":"Compute detection rates, false-positive and false-negative rates per mitigation arm; compare proportions with chi-squared or Fisher exact tests. Calculate precision, recall, and F1 relative to adjudicated ground truth. Report inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa). Analyze adversarial examples that bypassed mitigation to characterize failure modes and recommend policy enhancements.","novelty_evidence_ids":["doi:10.1145/3815174","https://openalex.org/W4401042853","https://openalex.org/W4415680272"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4415721798","https://openalex.org/W7161165783","https://openalex.org/W4400611559"],"risks":["Adversarial prompt construction may produce ethically sensitive or potentially harmful content; restrict to emulator-only experiments and follow safe-adversarial protocols.","Adjudication of 'unsafe' can be subjective; require dual adjudicators and tie-breaker rules.","Mitigations tested are prototypical and may not reflect production-grade defense effectiveness, limiting generalizability."],"estimated_model_calls":1600}]} for TypeAdapter(CandidateSet); 2 validation errors for CandidateSet
